pictures.scene: Cornelis Kruseman, Godsvrucht - a peasant family kneeling together in prayer at the wayside shrine under the great trees with the old woman's hands joined over her rosary, I call upon You O LORD, come quickly to me, hear my voice when I call to You
pictures.name: pd_kruseman_roep

pictures.scene: Pieter Lastman, The Sacrifice of Manoah - Manoah kneeling with both hands lifted high while the flame and the smoke of the offering go up from the altar and the angel rises in them, may my prayer be set before You like incense, my uplifted hands like the evening offering
pictures.name: pd_lastman_wierook

pictures.scene: Carel Fabritius, The Sentry - the soldier posted at the gateway sitting under the arch with his musket across his knees, set a guard O LORD over my mouth, keep watch at the door of my lips
pictures.name: pd_fabritius_wacht

pictures.scene: Anthony van Dyck, Saint Ambrose and the Emperor Theodosius - the bishop in his gold cope standing in the church door with his hand lifted to stop the emperor, who halts and opens his hands, let the righteous man strike me, let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion
pictures.name: pd_vandyck_bestraffing

pictures.scene: Gustave Courbet, The Etretat Cliffs after the Storm - the great white headland standing sheer above the sea with its arch and its needle of rock, when their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs
pictures.name: pd_courbet_rotsen

pictures.scene: Willem van Konijnenburg, Ploegende boer - the ploughman leaning on his plough with his ox over the broken clods and stones of the turned field, as when one plows and breaks up the soil, so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol
pictures.name: pd_konijnenburg_ploegen

pictures.scene: Bernardo Cavallino, Saint John the Evangelist - the saint with his eyes lifted and his hand raised in blessing over the chalice, but my eyes are fixed on You O GOD the Lord, in You I seek refuge
pictures.name: pd_cavallino_ogen

pictures.scene: Anthonie van Borssom, Landschap bij maneschijn - the long fishing net strung on its stakes across the dark foreground with a man tending it and the moon low behind the sailing barge, keep me from the snares they have laid for me, let the wicked fall into their own nets while I pass by in safety
pictures.name: pd_borssom_netten

lines.text: A Psalm of David.
I call upon You, O LORD; come quickly to me.
Hear my voice when I call to You.
May my prayer be set before You like incense;
my uplifted hands, like the evening offering.
Set a guard, O LORD, over my mouth;
keep watch at the door of my lips.
Do not let my heart be drawn to any evil thing
or take part in works of wickedness
with men who do iniquity;
let me not feast on their delicacies.
Let the righteous man strike me;
let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion.
It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it.
For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.
When their rulers are thrown down from the cliffs,
the people will listen to my words,
for they are pleasant.
As when one plows and breaks up the soil,
so our bones have been scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
But my eyes are fixed on You,
O GOD the Lord.
In You I seek refuge;
do not leave my soul defenseless.
Keep me from the snares they have laid for me,
and from the lures of evildoers.
Let the wicked fall into their own nets,
while I pass by in safety.
